sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Qazi Vakil Ahmad Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State and perused the record.

By means of this application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant Mohd. Faiyaz @ Faiyaz, who is involved in Case Crime No. 263 of 2022, under Sections 376, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act,
police station Noida Phase-2, district Gautambuddha Nagar, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.

As per prosecution case, in brief, the victim herself lodged the first information report of this case on 21.06.2022 against present applicant Faiyaz, Gulnaz and Farheen with the allegation inter alia that she had her birthday on 31.05.2021.
She invited her neighbour Farheen at her home and she came with her brother Faiyaz and introduced her to her brother.

Thereafter, Faiyaz asked his sister to Mohd. Faiyaz @ Faiyaz vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26401788/
1 return home and told her that he will come after some time.

sentences.text: Later, Faiyaz proposed her by saying that he started liking her and want to marry her.
Faiyaz gave her something mixed in cold-drink to drink, then she had no consciousness and Faiyaz committed misdeed with her and also made video.

The F.I.R. further alleges that the applicant extended threat by saying that if she tells anything to his sister or family members, then he will make her obscene photographs and video viral on the internet and on the said pretext, he made forceful physical relation with her.
The applicant also made promise to marry her but later on, the applicant and his family members refused for her marriage with the applicant.

Main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that though the victim had made allegation of rape against the applicant in the F.I.R. as well as in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. against him but when she was examined before the trial Court as PW-1 on 07.02.2023,
she has denied the incident in her examination-in-chief and has also stated inter alia that her uncle Sonu had obtained her signatures on a blank paper, on which he got the F.I.R. lodged under her name.
After examination-in-chief of the victim, she has been declared hostile at the request of the prosecution.

Referring the deposition of the victim recorded before the trial Court, it is argued that in the light of statement of the victim, there is bleak chance of conviction of the applicant, therefore,
the applicant, who is languishing in jail since 24.07.2022 is entitled to be released on bail.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant in the light of the allegation levelled against the applicant in the F.I.R. but he could not dispute the above factual aspect of the matter as argued on behalf of the applicant.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find substance in the submission of learned counsel for the applicant that the victim has completely denied the alleged incident and has been declared hostile.

She also made her uncle Sonu responsible to set the criminal law in motion by obtaining her signatures on a blank paper and to lodge the F.I.R. behind her back, therefore, the applicant has made out a prima facie case for bail.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant Mohd. Faiyaz @ Faiyaz, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions, which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) That the applicant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.
(ii) That the applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) That after his release, the applicant shall not involve in any criminal activity.
